### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`  _(via relatedLists (literal, a string literal in RELATED_LISTS_KEY))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx`  _(via relatedLists (literal, a string literal in RELATED_LISTS_KEY))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via relatedLists (literal, a string literal in RELATED_LISTS_KEY))_
- `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx`  _(via relatedLists (literal, a string literal in RELATED_LISTS_KEY))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via relatedLists (literal, a string literal in RELATED_LISTS_KEY))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7968e54be3d3e4f8f096523033151002daf549b2` — the merge of head `bc95079f79dd0b57d4782aab1cc53fc8dbbda6b6` into base `0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7968e54be3d3e4f8f096523033151002daf549b2 && git checkout 7968e54be3d3e4f8f096523033151002daf549b2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6 bc95079f79dd0b57d4782aab1cc53fc8dbbda6b6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6 && git merge --no-ff bc95079f79dd0b57d4782aab1cc53fc8dbbda6b6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT** at head `bc95079f79dd0b57d4782aab1cc53fc8dbbda6b6` (Fixes #37502). Full read · 2026-11-26T15:03Z

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.** `l1-face --pr 37596`: 12 of 13 items ok, one flag (below). Check-runs at bc95079f79: 57 success, 11 expected skip, 0 unexpected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending; `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` both success; mergeable_state clean. Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #37502`, no closing keyword next to another card. 4 files, +151/-13. Not governed. `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none` in the body and the changeset.

**The one flag is not a gap.** l1-face reports `@objectstack/cli` touched with no changeset. The only cli file is `packages/cli/test/starter-field-consumers.test.ts`, and cli's `files` is `dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md`, so nothing cli ships moves. The `@objectstack/lint` patch is the changeset that is owed.

**Fixes is right.** The card's three Done-when items are all in the diff: (1) an object-form `relatedLists` entry is read against the child its `list` names, so a parent field with the same name and no other consumer is reported; (2) the new `[#37502]` describe pins both directions (the parent's `phone` is still reported, and the child's own column counts); (3) `withoutPlacement` is narrowed back to related lists of the control's own object, and the blank-template control `blank_company.phone` now goes red on the unfixed lint dist (report: 1 failed / 24 passed) and green after (25/25).

**The change, read against main.**
- `walk` switches context only for a record at `objects` root, top-level `relatedLists` key, where `relatedListEntryName` answers. That is the spec's own reader (`packages/spec/src/data/related-list-entry.ts:82`), not a re-spelling. `RELATED_LISTS_KEY` is typed `satisfies keyof ServiceObject`, so a spec rename fails typecheck instead of turning the crediting off silently.
- Crediting columns to the child matches the published describe: "This list's columns, as field names of the child object" (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:1373`).
- An undeclared child (another package's or a platform object) answers `undefined`, so its columns land on no object and never on the parent. That is pinned.
- The `child.field` side effect is the same mechanism: the `list` token is now resolved against the child, where that relationship field is declared. It is pinned, and it under-reports nothing.

**Test evidence.** Real commands with counts: lint file 201/201, lint suite 9687/9687, typecheck exit 0. Positive control: ablation of the walk switch turns 4 of the 7 new cases red. The cli control was measured red before and green after on origin/main c385d3bd1.

**Dev deviations, judged.**
- ADR-0139 D4: the dev is right. D4 is "The six consumers emit one leaf per parent object, and no pre-scan" (engine semi-join / plugin-audit read gate, `docs/adr/0139-…md:251`). It says nothing about lint crediting, so there is no conflict and no fork.
- Severity stays `warning`. The rule now reports one more true miss and stops one false report. `os validate --strict` turns warnings into exit 1, so a stack that has exactly this miss would newly fail `--strict`. That is an opt-in lint finding, not a refusal by the published schema or the metadata door, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed. The sweep shows no new warning in app-crm, app-starter, the blank template or app-todo. app-showcase and app-multi-package declare no object-form `relatedLists` entry in their sources (only a showcase test names the word), so neither can move.
- The new pins sit in the existing test file (AGENTS.md shared-harness rule): accepted.

**Changeset, sentence by sentence.** An object-form entry is read against the child (true, `walk`). Before, a column credited the parent's same-name field, and the blank starter's `company.phone` stayed quiet (true, the cli control). `os validate` / `os lint` can newly report such a parent field, and a child field that only a related list draws is no longer reported (true, both pinned). A column of an undeclared child credits no object (true, pinned). The rule stays a warning (true, no severity line moves). `child.field` counts as a read of that relationship field on the child (true, pinned).

**Contract review.** None owed. No `packages/spec/src/**` file, no governed path, no `Clause-②: yes`, no narrowing declared. CI plus this read cover it (contract-review.md: four faces untouched).

**Out of scope (dev note).** An entry with no `columns` draws the child FK's `relatedListColumns` or the derived columns, and the rule does not credit those. This under-credits, which is the quiet direction, and is unchanged here. Not filed: it is noted in the PR's Acceptance notes, and no observed false report pulls for it.

**Landing:** not governed, ≤3000 lines, no narrowing. The area lands it (landing-operations). `Fixes` closes the card, so no manual `pm:dispatched` strip is owed.
